text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages with eight quote variants each, for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Harrowgate Protection Desk in Kelemba Camp opened 1,248 new case files for refugees with specific protection needs. Our six caseworkers conducted an average of 14 home visits per week, prioritising unaccompanied children and survivors of violence. Referral pathways to the camp health post were strengthened, and 82% of urgent referrals were completed within 48 hours. However, the planned expansion to Block D did not go ahead because the site was never formally allocated by camp management. We are grateful to the Linden Trust for its continued flexibility, which allowed us to redirect funds toward interpreter costs when two languages were added to the caseload in September.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the third quarter of 2024 for the Sunbright Playgroup Network across Maro District. Twenty-three playgroups were active, each meeting twice a week under the guidance of trained parent facilitators. Attendance averaged 17 children per session, slightly above the target of 15. Observation visits found that 64% of sessions included a structured storytelling activity, compared with 41% in the previous quarter. Facilitators reported that low-cost play kits made from local materials were popular with caregivers. No playgroup was closed during the period, although two groups in Tembe village did not meet for three weeks during the flooding in August.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Kestrel Basic Needs Fund delivered monthly cash transfers to 3,400 households in the Orun Valley, an increase of 600 on the previous year. Each household received the equivalent of 45 dollars, transferred through mobile money agents in eleven market towns. Post-distribution monitoring showed that 71% of recipients spent most of the transfer on food, followed by school fees and medicine. Households headed by women reported eating two meals a day more often than before enrolment. Transfers were not interrupted at any point, even when fuel shortages closed the main road in March. We did not observe significant price inflation in the monitored markets, which suggests local traders were able to meet the additional demand.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Calder Springs Rural Water Project aimed to drill 12 boreholes in Nyasi Ward by the end of June 2024. To date, nine boreholes have been completed and handed over to village water committees, and all nine passed water quality tests. Latrine construction has moved more slowly: 140 household latrines have been built against a target of 250. The delay is not due to funding but to a shortage of masons during the harvest season. Committees have collected maintenance fees in seven of the nine villages. The remaining three boreholes will not be drilled until the hydrogeological survey for Lusi and Pembe is repeated, as the first survey wasn't conclusive.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the volunteer trainer team at the Brightwater Skills Centre in Okoro. Each cohort has 20 trainees aged between 18 and 24, and the course runs for twelve weeks. Please arrive at least 15 minutes before your session so that tools can be checked and signed out. Trainees should never operate the welding equipment without a qualified instructor in the room. In past cohorts, about 60% of graduates found paid work within six months, and many told us that patient volunteers made the difference. Do not give trainees your personal phone number; all contact outside sessions goes through the centre coordinator. If a trainee misses two sessions in a row, record it in the attendance log so that staff can follow up.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Willowmere Family Links Service supported 87 children in temporary foster placements across Ranza Province. Caseworkers completed family tracing for 52 of these children, and 31 have since been reunified with a parent or relative. Every reunified child received at least two follow-up visits in the first month. The service did not place any child under five in a residential institution during the reporting period. Foster carers attended monthly peer support meetings, with average attendance of 78%. Delays in tracing were most often linked to missing birth records, and in nine cases no relatives could be found despite repeated searches.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation of the Lanternlight Evening Literacy Network was carried out in October 2023, eighteen months into a three-year programme. The network runs 34 classes in church halls and schools across Dulani County, with most learners being women over 30. Reading assessments showed that 58% of learners could read a short paragraph aloud, up from 12% at baseline. Learners valued the evening timing, which did not conflict with farm work. However, facilitators have not received refresher training since the launch, and several classes lack enough primers. The evaluators recommend that the network prioritises facilitator support before opening new classes.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Greystone Community Paralegal Programme covered its first 24 months of operation in the Hollin and Marsh districts. Over this period, 16 paralegals handled 2,130 cases, most involving land disputes, inheritance and unpaid wages. Roughly two in five cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Clients interviewed by the evaluation team said paralegals explained their rights clearly, and 89% said they would recommend the service. The evaluation found that the referral link with the district legal aid office was not functioning, and lawyers rarely took up complex cases. Paralegals also noted that they were never reimbursed for travel to remote villages in the first year.

passages.source_passage: The Ashfield Wellbeing Collective has provided community-based counselling in the Tarn Hills since 2019. Following the landslides of 2022, demand for support rose sharply, and our waiting list now exceeds 300 people. A household survey we conducted last year found that 37% of adults reported symptoms of persistent distress, yet fewer than one in ten had ever spoken to a counsellor. Stigma remains a major barrier, and many families do not consider emotional difficulties a health concern. Our eight lay counsellors are trained in problem-solving therapy and supervised weekly by a clinical psychologist. This proposal seeks funding to train twelve additional counsellors and open two satellite sites in villages that currently have no psychosocial services.

passages.source_passage: This update summarises progress on the Redfern Malaria Shield campaign in Kasoro and Bendi districts as of 30 April 2024. Distribution teams have delivered 58,000 long-lasting insecticidal nets, reaching 91% of registered households. Registration took longer than planned because census lists were not up to date in several villages. Spot checks one month after distribution found nets hanging in four out of five homes visited. No stock losses have been reported from the district warehouses. The board should note that the second phase, covering the lakeshore communities, cannot begin until the rainy season ends in June.
